'''''Luculia gratissima''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Rubiaceae]]. It is an [[ornamental plant]] that is found from the central [[Himalayas]] to northern [[Indo-China]].<ref name="WCSP">{{cite web|url=https://apps.kew.org/wcsp/qsearch.do?plantName=Luculia|title=''Luculia'' in the World Checklist of Rubiaceae|accessdate=20 July 2012}}</ref>

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''gratissima'' means "most pleasing" or "most agreeable".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref> 

It is a large [[shrub]] or even a small tree growing to {{convert|4|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|1.5|m|ft|abbr=on}} broad, with pointed ribbed leaves, and clustered fragrant pale pink flowers in autumn and winter. As it does not tolerate temperatures below {{convert|5|C|F|abbr=on}}, it requires cultivation under glass in [[temperate climate|temperate]] zones. However, it may be placed outside in a sheltered, sunny spot during the summer months. It is a recipient of the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/89320/Luculia-gratissima/Details | title = ''Luculia gratissima'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 25 December 2020}}</ref>
